clue.text: Trained lawyer taken in by infants talks like them

indicators.note: being taken in by something means being held inside it, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: babes are infants
BL, Bachelor of Law, is the degree of a trained lawyer

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trained lawyer surrounded by small children, chattering away as they do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'them' points back to the infants, so the definition means talks as little children do.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies make meaningless chattering sounds, so to talk like infants is to prattle incoherently.

clue.text: Retiring punch-drunk!

explanation.surface: A boxer, shy and also reeling from too many blows.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a joke: someone punch-drunk is full of bashes, read as BASH + FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy; humorously, punch-drunk means full of punches, with bash meaning a blow.

clue.text: Did it fly from Eden?

parts.note: imagines a winged creature that took off from the Garden of Eden, the biblical paradise

explanation.surface: A question about some creature leaving the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: This brightly plumed tropical species is named for paradise, which Eden is in the Bible.

clue.text: Put down face up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: An instruction to place something with its front showing.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning placed or set down.

clue.text: Balls renowned for ethereal music

explanation.surface: Some globes have a reputation for heavenly melodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The music of the spheres was an ancient idea of harmony made by the moving planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Globes are round balls; the ancient heavenly orbs were said to produce celestial harmony as they turned.

clue.text: A victim of 25 who sounded fit and 24

indicators.note: the victim's name, when spoken, is said like another word, signalling a homophone

parts.note: fit means capable, and 24 down's answer is the same word meaning competent

explanation.surface: A victim who seemed healthy enough, by the sound of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 25 is CAIN, who killed his brother in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the first murder is of Adam's second son, killed by his elder brother.

clue.text: Offence caused by priest breaking a holy water vessel

indicators.note: the priest breaks into the vessel, splitting it so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a font holds holy water for baptism
Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest

explanation.surface: A cleric smashes a church basin and causes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: An insult or slight that gives offence is an affront.

clue.text: Why the Home Rule politician abandoned the Empire?

definitions.text: Why the Home Rule politician abandoned the Empire?

indicators.note: the politician leaves the word Empire, so those letters are taken away from it

parts.note: taken as written
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: A history question about why an Irish nationalist walked out of the British Empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Home Rule was the campaign for Irish self-government; the remaining name is the Irish state that eventually left.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish Free State took this Gaelic name for Ireland in 1937, achieving self-rule outside the Empire.

clue.text: Draw up again by vermilion and maroon craft

parts.note: vermilion is a shade of red
a raft is the craft a marooned castaway builds

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of colours: vermilion and maroon for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maroon' looks like another colour after vermilion, but it is the verb to strand someone on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To write a new version of a document is to draw it up again.

clue.text: Ice-hockey tour a mix-up, so pick whichever you want

indicators.note: a mix-up jumbles things, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ice-hockey tour has gone wrong, so you can choose any option.
explanation.definitionFit: An invitation to make any selection one likes.

clue.text: Honest description of where anxious hospital visitor heads

definitions.text: description of where anxious hospital visitor heads

explanation.surface: A worried visitor rushes to a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second sense as STRAIGHT FOR WARD: the anxious visitor heads directly to the ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and direct people are honest; going directly towards a hospital ward is heading straight for it.

clue.text: It hops under a horse's hoof

explanation.surface: Something jumps beneath a horse's foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The frog is also the soft triangular pad on the underside of a horse's hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: An amphibian moves by jumping; farriers use the same name for the elastic pad on the sole of a hoof.

clue.text: Crime for which a parson is beheaded

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the head, so the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman is executed for some offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: He an Egyptian deity, she an Olympian one

parts.note: taken as written
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A comparison of a male Egyptian god with a female Greek goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: The queen of the gods on Mount Olympus, wife of Zeus, is a female deity.

clue.text: Musical items illustrating compositional inversion

indicators.note: inversion is turning around; the word illustrates it by reading the same when its composition is inverted

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Pieces of music show a technique of turning melody upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inversion' sounds musical, but the clue means the word itself spelt backwards stays the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces performed by a single musician are musical items.

clue.text: Colour common in the village

explanation.surface: A shade often found in rural places.
explanation.walkthrough: A village green is the common grassy land at the heart of an English village.
explanation.definitionFit: Grass has this hue; an area of shared open grass in a village is called by the same name.

clue.text: Greyhounds? No, much smaller breeds

parts.note: greyhounds race round a track lapping it, but these are tiny pets that sit on a knee

explanation.surface: A dog lover corrects someone: not big racing dogs but tiny ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pet breeds kept to sit on an owner's knee are named for that perch.

clue.text: Evict all the people who attend

explanation.surface: An order to throw out everyone who comes along.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel someone from a home is to put them out; the number attending an event is its attendance.

clue.text: Drawing a ring enclosed in a box

indicators.note: the ring is placed inside the box, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard box
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A drawing of a ring inside a packing box.
explanation.definitionFit: A humorous sketch or comic strip picture is a type of drawing.

clue.text: It is practised on heated locks and frozen lochs

definitions.text: It is practised on heated locks and frozen lochs

parts.words: It is practised on heated locks and frozen lochs
parts.note: one activity uses tongs on hair, the other is a Scottish stone-sliding game on ice

explanation.surface: Something done to hair with hot tongs and on Scottish ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Lochs are Scottish lakes; the ice game with stones and brooms began in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair is wound with hot tongs into ringlets, and a winter sport slides stones across ice; both share one name.

clue.text: A person who is certainly not sharp

definitions.text: A person who is certainly not sharp

parts.words: A person who is certainly not sharp
parts.note: a gifted person born with talent, but read musically as a note neither sharp nor flat

explanation.surface: A remark about someone who is rather dim.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical note that is neither sharp nor flat bears this name, as does someone innately gifted.

clue.text: Got over the accusation apparently

explanation.surface: Someone has overcome a charge, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: A horse gets over a fence by jumping it; someone acquitted has got rid of the charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping a hurdle without touching it means getting over it; acquittal frees a person from the charge.

clue.text: Corroborate what an embezzler on the staff is likely to do

definitions.text: what an embezzler on the staff is likely to do

explanation.surface: A dishonest employee is likely to back up a story.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second sense as CON FIRM: the embezzler swindles the company.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify or support a claim is to corroborate it; a thieving employee would cheat the business.

clue.text: Send mad renewed requests of an importunate nature

indicators.note: renewing makes something afresh, so these letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sends crazy repeated pleas.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent, pressing calls for something are firm claims.

clue.text: Where in the Isle of Wight one hears what horsemen do

definitions.text: Where in the Isle of Wight

indicators.note: says that the answer is the spoken form of the words that follow

parts.note: horsemen ride horses

explanation.surface: A question about a place on the Isle of Wight and riders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Wight is an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is the island's main ferry port on its north-east coast, a place on the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Make amends and be united

explanation.surface: Apologise and come together.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word for the first sense, and as two words AT ONE for the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To make reparation for wrongdoing is to expiate; being in harmony with someone is being in agreement.

clue.text: Which letter of mine represents the others?

definitions.text: Which letter of mine represents the others?

parts.words: Which letter of mine represents the others?
parts.note: the opening letter of the word mine, read as the letter, says a pronoun for other people

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking which character in a word stands for other people.
explanation.walkthrough: Asked which letter of 'mine', reply 'the M', which sounds like a pronoun for other people.
explanation.definitionFit: A plural pronoun for other people, set against us, is the reply to the riddle.

clue.text: Competent as a follower immersed in liquor

indicators.note: being immersed in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ale is a brewed liquor
B follows A in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A capable assistant who has been soaked in drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable and skilled people are competent.

clue.text: One in prison was a marked man

indicators.note: one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in jail was a targeted man.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis, God put a mark on the man who killed his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical murderer was branded with a sign by God, making him literally marked.

clue.text: Serving as Polaris crewman before appointment to ministry leads to insolence

parts.note: Polaris missiles were carried on submarines, so a crewman serves in a sub
ordination is the appointment of a person to the Christian ministry

explanation.surface: A sailor on a nuclear submarine who later becomes a cleric turns rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Polaris was the nuclear missile carried by British and US submarines.
explanation.definitionFit: Defiance of authority and disobedience amounts to insolence.

clue.text: Bounder employed any bounder

explanation.surface: A cad who is used by anyone who jumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Bounder is old British slang for a cad; anyone bounding along uses the back of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or scoundrel is a bounder; the back part of the foot is used by anyone who jumps.

clue.text: Politeness shown by married woman accommodating Princess Royal

indicators.note: accommodating means housing or holding, so the title goes around the name

parts.note: Mrs is the title of a married woman
Anne is the current Princess Royal, the King's sister

explanation.surface: A wife displays courtesy to a royal visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Princess Royal is a British title held by the monarch's eldest daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Good social behaviour and courtesy are what one's etiquette shows.
